I can't believe these people took the idea of "British people saying anything sounds like an insult" and turned it into a game. Furthermore, it's a really fun one.

I think weaknesses, combos, and specific character phrases do a good job at keeping this game fresh for longer than you would expect. I've played over 70 duels and I'm still finding new phrases and silly wordplay, and there's a fun meta surrounding which phrases work with what and when to take an "and" or keep going with an insult. The character roster is inspired for how small it is, with everyone having some unique accent to say sentences in their own delightful way (Albert is probably my favorite in this regard, though Lo Wang's "Says the fortune cookie!" gets me too).

Of course this isn't going to be the type of game I play all the time given its limited gameplay loop, but I'm having a fun time randomly getting achievements and winning tournaments with everyone. This game is a bit of a novelty, but a unique one at that and it does what it set out to do very well.

[i]Oh...Sire!! The Insult Simulator[/i] is an extremely simple game that is probably a really fun party game with friends, but isn't worth your time if you're only interested in the singleplayer.

Mechanically the game consists of taking turns to construct your insult from fragments of sentences, drawing from a shared pool of ten fragments plus up to four bonus fragments you don't share with you opponent. The strategy comes from balancing how aggressively you want to play (since longer and more complicated insults will usually score higher, but have a higher chance of being interrupted by your opponent picking a fragment you need to finish it), while also choosing fragments which will prevent your opponent from making the best insult they can (for example by preventing them from building a combo, or from selecting topics that your character is 'weak' to). This is fun, but extremely shallow. Unless you get very unlucky with the sentence fragments you get given you will almost never need to worry about losing to the ai, and games will become very repetitive very quickly. I imagine it would be great with friends and could lead to a lot of fun mindgames, but I'm only reviewing this from a singleplayer pov. 

The game also doesn't deliver on what the title promises. 'Insult simulator' probably makes you imagine something like the famous insult duel from [i]The Secret of Monkey Island[/i]. Nothing could be further from what the game actually is. 90% of the time the AI will spit out insults that are complete nonsense or are even compliments. When the insults they spit out do work they're still boring and repetitive. The AI is too basic and the rules for insult construction too restrictive to produce much entertainment. This is another aspect of the game which wouldn't be a problem in multiplayer, but completely sinks the singleplayer experience.
